prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You are an expert agent in advanced hierarchical and compositional planning using foundation models.

User request:
Plan a detailed mission for a Mars rover involving geological surveying and sample collection. The rover has to navigate the terrain, identify geological features of interest, collect samples, and transmit data back to Earth.

Initial State: The rover is landed on a predetermined site on Mars with varied terrain features and geological diversity. It is equipped with navigation, sampling, and communication tools.

Goal: Conduct a comprehensive geological survey of the area and collect samples from at least three distinct geological features, then prepare and transmit a detailed report of findings back to Earth.
answer:
# MARS ROVER GEOLOGICAL SURVEY & SAMPLE RETURN-CACHE MISSION PLAN
## Mission designation: *STRATA-1* (Survey, Traverse, Retrieve, Analyze, Transmit Autonomously)

---

## 1. Mission Goal Decomposition

The user-level goal is decomposed recursively into a **hierarchy of goals, phases, tasks, and primitive actions**. Each level inherits the postconditions of its children (HTN-style: a task is achieved when all ordered subtasks complete and their combined effects satisfy the parent's postcondition).

```
G0  (Mission) Complete geological survey + ≥3 distinct samples + transmitted report
├── G1  Safe, calibrated, mobile rover                     [Sol 0–5]
├── G2  Characterized landing-site geology & target list   [Sol 6–10]
├── G3  ≥3 distinct geological units surveyed in situ      [Sol 11–52]
├── G4  ≥3 samples acquired from ≥3 distinct units         [Sol 11–52]
├── G5  Samples documented, sealed, cached                 [continuous]
├── G6  Findings synthesized into a validated report       [Sol 53–70]
├── G7  Report transmitted, receipt confirmed, archived    [Sol 71–78]
└── G8  (Cross-cutting) Power, thermal, data, and health invariants maintained
```

**Measurable success criteria (G0 acceptance test):**
| # | Criterion | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Geological units sampled | ≥ 3, each independently corroborated by ≥2 instruments |
| C2 | Total sealed samples | ≥ 5 (redundancy ≥ 1 extra per unit; 1 optional 4th unit) |
| C3 | Sample documentation completeness | 100% of samples with pre/post imaging, hole geometry, mineralogy, context |
| C4 | Report delivered | Full report + raw data bundle acknowledged by DSN/relay |
| C5 | Rover health | Nominal power, thermal, mobility at end of mission |
| C6 | Contamination control | ≥ 2 witness blanks unopened and returned to cache |

**Graceful-degradation success:** If mobility or power degrades, mission is still "successful" at C1 = 2 units + C3 + C4 (partial-credit objective).

---

## 2. Assumptions, Inventory, and Constraints

**Initial state (given):** rover on surface at Site LS-1, nominal health after landing; navigation, sampling (drill + arm + cache), and communication (UHF relay + X-band DTE) suites available; terrain heterogeneous.

**Working assumptions (to verify in Sol 0–5):**
- Landing ellipse contains ≥ 3 distinct units within a 3 km traverse radius.
- Orbiter relay passes ≥ 2 per sol, total downlink ≥ 1.5 GB/sol.
- Power: RTG, ~110 W EOL continuous, 42 Ah battery, ~450 Wh/sol usable.
- Driving: ≤ 100 m/sol ground-planned, ≤ 25 m/sol autonomous-hazard; solar-array/RTG-thermal margin ≥ 20%.
- Drill: 1 sample tube per ~2 sols including analysis; 38 tubes total, reserve 20 for this mission.

**Hard constraints:** slope ≤ 30° (traverse), ≤ 20° (drill site); arm reach workspace free of >5 cm rocks; no driving with arm unstowed; uplink window lead time ≥ 1 sol for ground-planned sequences.

---

## 3. Phase-Level Plan (Level 1)

### PHASE P0 — Commissioning & Calibration (Sol 0–5) → satisfies G1

| Task | Actions (Level 3 primitives) | Preconditions | Postconditions |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0.1 Post-landing health check | Deploy high-gain antenna; downlink housekeeping; poll fault log; exit safe mode | Rover awake | Faults cleared, state known |
| P0.2 Mobility validation | Unstow mast & arm; short 5 m drive; verify wheel currents, steering, odometry vs. visual odometry | P0.1 | Driving achievable; slip model baseline |
| P0.3 Instrument calibration | Pan-cam flat-field & geometric calibration; laser spectrometer on calibration target; drill feed test on inert coupon | P0.2 | Instruments certified |
| P0.4 Comms baseline | X-band DTE link test; UHF relay pass test; confirm data rates | P0.1 | Link budget confirmed |
| P0.5 Localization | Star/sun-fix + orbital image matching; establish site frame | P0.1 | Rover position known ±2 m |

**Exit gate:** all four subsystems certified nominal, else enter Contingency Branch A (Section 7).

---

### PHASE P1 — Regional Survey & Target Selection (Sol 6–10) → satisfies G2

| Task | Actions | Output |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 360° panorama | Mast pan (36 frames), stereo depth mosaic, zoom on 6 candidate outcrops | Context mosaic |
| P1.2 Orbital data fusion | Register HiRISE/CRISM-style orbital mineralogy + DEM to local frame; build traverse cost map (slope, rock abundance, sand traps) | Cost map + unit map |
| P1.3 Remote spectroscopy | Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy + passive reflectance on 6–10 candidate targets | Preliminary compositions |
| P1.4 Subsurface sounding | Ground-penetrating radar lines over 3 candidate areas | Stratigraphy depth profile |
| P1.5 **Target list generation** | Rank candidates by (a) mineralogical distinctness, (b) accessibility, (c) stratigraphic value, (d) drillability | Ordered target list T1…T8 with rationale |
| P1.6 Traverse plan + FIDO check | Plan P1→T1 path; simulate energy/data/sol budget; submit for ground approval | Approved sol sequence |

**Decision rule for "distinctness" (C1):** two units are distinct if they differ by ≥ 2 of: dominant mineral class (e.g., olivine vs. hydrated silica vs. sulfate), stratigraphic position, grain size/texture class, or geochemical ratio (e.g., Fe/Mg). Documented per target.

**Baseline unit hypothesis (illustrative, verified in P1):**
- **U1 — Olivine-rich basaltic bedrock** (mantle-derived, low alteration)
- **U2 — Clay/hydrated-silica layered unit** (aqueous alteration, possible habitability)
- **U3 — Sulfate-bearing vein network** (fluid-flow record, fracture mineralization)
- **U4 (optional) — Impact ejecta / conglomerate** (provenance & chronology)

---

### PHASE P2 — Survey & Sampling Campaign (Sol 11–52) → satisfies G3, G4, G5

Executed as a **repeating compositional subroutine** — `SURVEY_AND_SAMPLE(Unit U, Budget B)` — instantiated once per distinct unit. Each instantiation is a method with its own precondition/effect contract.

```
METHOD SURVEY_AND_SAMPLE(U):
  precondition: rover at safe standoff <50 m from U; power ≥ 60%; ≥2 tubes free
  1. TRAVERSE_TO(U)                → rover in drill workspace
  2. CHARACTERIZE(U)               → unit certified distinct
  3. SELECT_SAMPLE_POINT(U)        → target point with 20°-slope, arm-reachable
  4. ACQUIRE_SAMPLE(U)             → sealed tube + tailings
  5. DOCUMENT_SAMPLE(U)            → full metadata record
  6. CACHE_AND_STOW()              → tube indexed in cache
  7. DOWNLINK_UPLINK_SOL(U)        → data on Earth, ground concurrence on next unit
  postcondition: unit sampled, documented, cached, ground-approved
```

| Sub-task | Key actions | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| P2.1 `TRAVERSE_TO` | Ground-planned drive legs (≤ 100 m/sol), hazard-avoid auto-nav on terminal 20 m, slip check every 10 m, arm stowed | 2–6 sols/unit |
| P2.2 `CHARACTERIZE` | Mast imaging, laser chemistry grid (9 points), microscopic imager, XRD/mineralogy, GPR contact line; **verify distinctness vs. previously sampled units** | 2–3 sols |
| P2.3 `SELECT_SAMPLE_POINT` | Abrasion test on 2 candidates; rank by freshness, homogeneity, accessibility; confirm no arm collision | 1 sol |
| P2.4 `ACQUIRE_SAMPLE` | Drill 1 core (~5 cm); capture tailings; image borehole; seal tube; verify seal telemetry | 1–2 sols |
| P2.5 `DOCUMENT_SAMPLE` | Pre/post images, hole geometry, depth, mass estimate, mineralogy, context mosaic, contamination log | 0.5 sol |
| P2.6 `CACHE_AND_STOW` | Transfer tube to carousel; record index; verify latch | 0.5 sol |
| P2.7 Optional second sample per unit | Only if first sample is anomalous or margin allows | +2 sols |

**Sampling schedule (nominal, with float):**

| Unit | Sols | Samples | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| U1 Bedrock | 11–20 | 2 (S1, S2) | First unit; also validates drill end-to-end |
| U2 Clay/silica layered | 23–33 | 2 (S3, S4) | Highest biosignature value → extra replicate |
| U3 Sulfate veins | 36–46 | 1–2 (S5, S6) | Vein may be thin → choose vein-rich outcrop |
| U4 (optional) | 48–52 | 1 (S7) | Only if schedule float ≥ 3 sols and power ≥ 70% |

**Contamination protocol (G5 invariant):** witness blanks loaded pre-launch; open only the tube being filled; document all arm/bit contacts; keep one sealed blank reserved for return.

---

### PHASE P3 — Closeout Survey & Data Synthesis (Sol 53–70) → satisfies G6

| Task | Actions |
|---|---|
| P3.1 Closeout survey | Re-image sampled sites from a distance; complete remaining GPR/remote-sensing lines; fill gaps in unit map |
| P3.2 Data reduction | Ground team processes spectra, chemistry, stratigraphy; cross-calibrate against orbital data |
| P3.3 Hypothesis testing | Evaluate: (a) aqueous alteration history, (b) habitability indicators, (c) stratigraphic correlations, (d) sample representativeness |
| P3.4 Report authoring | Structured report: context, methods, unit descriptions, sample log, data tables, interpretations, uncertainties, recommendations for next mission |
| P3.5 Peer/QA review | Internal review; verify every claim traceable to a data product ID; check sample manifest vs. physical cache |

---

### PHASE P4 — Transmission & Verification (Sol 71–78) → satisfies G7

| Task | Actions |
|---|---|
| P4.1 Tiered downlink | Tier 1: report text + summary tables + key images. Tier 2: full data products. Tier 3: raw/archival bundle |
| P4.2 Redundancy | Transmit via ≥ 2 relay passes + 1 DTE pass; use retransmit on any CRC failure |
| P4.3 Receipt confirmation | Ground acknowledges each tier; rover logs ACK; re-send missing blocks |
| P4.4 Archive & audit | Ground archives bundle; reconciles sample manifest; publishes sol-by-sol activity log |
| P4.5 End-state report | Rover health status + cache state + final position for future mission planning |

**Data budget:** ~1.5 GB/sol relay × 60 sols ≈ 90 GB total downlink capacity; report bundle ~2 GB; raw science data ~40 GB — margin ≈ 2×.

---

## 4. Operational Cadence (Ground-in-the-Loop)

| Time (local) | Activity |
|---|---|
| Sol start | Downlink housekeeping + previous sol science data via orbiter |
| +2 h | Ground: plan next sol sequence, simulate, uplink |
| Mid-sol | Rover executes autonomous sequence; onboard fault protection may halt and safemode |
| Late sol | UHF relay pass: downlink compressed telemetry + critical images |
| Continuous | Rover autonomy loop: hazard detection, slip monitoring, power/thermal watchdogs |

**Autonomy envelope:** rover may autonomously re-plan within a sol for (a) hazard avoidance, (b) short target repositioning, (c) safemode recovery, (d) skipping a blocked waypoint. It may **not** autonomously drill, unstow the arm on unverified terrain, or change the target list.

---

## 5. Resource Budgets (nominal, 90-sol horizon)

| Resource | Budget | Planned use | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sols | 90 (78 planned + 12 contingency) | 78 | 15% |
| Energy | ~450 Wh/sol | Drive 120 Wh, instruments 140 Wh, comms 60 Wh, thermal 80 Wh, idle 50 Wh | ~20% |
| Drive distance | ~3.5 km capability | ~2.4 km planned | 30% |
| Sample tubes | 20 reserved | 6–7 used | 65% |
| Downlink | ~90 GB | ~45 GB | 50% |
| Arm/drill cycles | 40 | 12 | 70% |

---

## 6. Verification & Checkpoints (Gate Reviews)

| Gate | Sol | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| **G-A** Commissioning | 5 | All subsystems nominal, slip model valid |
| **G-B** Target list approved | 10 | ≥ 3 distinct units confirmed, traverse feasible |
| **G-C** Mid-campaign | 33 | 2 units sampled, ≥ 4 sols float remaining, power ≥ 50% |
| **G-D** Sampling complete | 52 | ≥ 5 samples from ≥ 3 units, manifest consistent |
| **G-E** Report QA | 70 | All claims traceable, manifest reconciled |
| **G-F** Transmission verified | 78 | All tiers ACK'd by ground |

If **G-C fails**, invoke Contingency Branch C (drop U4, compress characterization to 1 sol/unit).

---

## 7. Contingency Branches

| Branch | Trigger | Response |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Commissioning fault** | Instrument or drive failure at Sol ≤ 5 | Isolate failed subsystem; re-plan survey using remaining instruments; if drill fails → mission degrades to survey-only + report (C1 waived, C3/C4 retained) |
| **B — Traverse blocked** | Hazard field or slope > 30° on planned path | Re-plan with cost map; accept +3 sols; if no route, substitute nearest distinct unit |
| **C — Schedule slip** | Float < 3 sols at G-C | Drop U4; reduce characterization to 1 sol; prioritize U2 replicate |
| **D — Drill jam / seal fail** | Drill or tube seal fault | Abort that sample; relocate 1 m and retry once; if repeated, mark unit "surveyed, not sampled" and proceed to next unit |
| **E — Power/thermal anomaly** | Power < 30% or heater fault | Enter low-power mode: no driving, minimal uplink; resume when recovered; if unrecoverable → P4 transmission only (report from existing data) |
| **F — Comm failure** | No relay contact for 3 sols | Autonomous safe-hold, retry all passes, log data; escalate to DTE-only mode |
| **G — Loss of distinctness** | Two candidate units prove identical | Re-rank target list; add next candidate from T-list (must still meet C1) |

**Re-planning rule:** any branch that consumes > 3 sols triggers a full plan repair from the highest unaffected goal node, not a local patch — to preserve global feasibility (energy/data/sol constraints).

---

## 8. Risk Register (top items)

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sand trap immobilization | Medium | High | Cost map avoidance, slip monitoring, ≤ 25 m autonomous legs |
| Drill bit wear / jam | Medium | High | Abrasion tests first, spare bit, 1 retry per site |
| Sample contamination | Low | High | Witness blanks, sealed single-use tubes, documented contacts |
| Downlink shortfall | Low | Medium | Tiered priority transmission, 2× data margin |
| Thermal excursion | Low | High | Heater watchdogs, no driving in coldest window |
| Unit misidentification | Medium | Medium | Require 2-instrument corroboration before sampling |

---

## 9. Final Deliverables

1. **Geological survey report** — unit map, stratigraphy, mineralogy/chemistry tables, alteration & habitability interpretation, uncertainty analysis.
2. **Sample manifest** — per-sample: unit, coordinates, sol, depth, mineralogy, images, contamination record, cache index.
3. **Raw data bundle** — spectra, images, GPR, chemistry, housekeeping, sol activity log.
4. **Traverse & operations log** — every drive, decision, and replan with rationale.
5. **Rover end-state report** — health, position, cache contents, and recommendations for follow-on mission.

---

## 10. One-Line Summary

The rover commissions and calibrates (Sol 0–5), surveys the region and ranks distinct geological units using remote sensing plus orbital data fusion (Sol 6–10), then executes a repeatable **survey-and-sample subroutine** across at least three geologically distinct units — basaltic bedrock, clay/hydrated-silica layered rock, and sulfate veins — acquiring ≥ 5 sealed, fully documented samples with witness-blank contamination control (Sol 11–52), before synthesizing a traceable report (Sol 53–70) and transmitting it in verified tiers back to Earth (Sol 71–78), all within a 90-sol budget with ~15% schedule and ~20% power margin and explicit contingency branches at every gate.
